scenes.title: Read a geographic county map
scenes.learnerAction: On the supplied outline map, trace each county boundary and match its number to the key. Distinguish the county area from its administrative capital name.

content.body: Use the packet's Liberia county outline map, numbered key and north arrow. The outlines derive from pinned UNMIL/OCHA geographic coordinates via geoBoundaries, with CC BY 3.0 IGO attribution. Numbers identify county areas, not capital positions. Use the geographic outline for location tasks and the separate key for capital names.

scenes.title: Learn county areas and capitals
scenes.learnerAction: Find county numbers 8, 10 and 12 on the map. Name each county and copy its capital. Describe which lies farthest north.

content.body: The capital is the seat of county administration, not automatically the largest or best-known city. Montserrado's capital is Bensonville, also called Bentol. Monrovia is Liberia's national capital. Nimba's capital is Sanniquellie; Ganta is a different town. Use the geographic outline to find the county areas, then the separate register for recall.

scenes.title: Separate recall from spatial evidence
scenes.learnerAction: For each map number 1 through 15, write the county and capital. Then check against the key and correct missed pairs. Use the outline to decide whether Lofa or Maryland lies farther north and whether Maryland touches the coast. Explain how the north arrow and boundary support your answer.

content.body: Work first from the numbered outline without the key. Use a second copy with the key to check only after answering. A county-capital table can check names, while geographic outlines support coastal location and relative position. Capital points and roads are not drawn on this map.

scenes.title: Bound a geographic claim
scenes.learnerAction: Explain why the map can support a north-south comparison but the name register alone cannot.

content.body: A geographic outline shows where county areas lie. Its labels do not establish roads, passability or which capitals a road passes. A capital may lie away from a route through its county. Give separate reasons for an administrative name and a spatial claim.

items.prompt: Can this map establish a delivery road from Gbarnga to Harper?

options.text: No. It shows county areas but no roads or capital points.
options.feedback: Use current road data and capital coordinates to plan actual travel.

options.text: Yes. Joining the county numbers gives the road.
options.feedback: County numbers are identifiers. Their order has no geographic or transport meaning.

scenes.title: Use geography without inventing a route
scenes.learnerAction: Name the data you need before claiming which counties and capitals a road passes. Do not guess a route from county numbers.

content.body: Synthetic school exchange: one school is in Lofa and another is in Maryland. Identify both administrative capitals. Use the outline to explain their relative location and which county is coastal. Then request the additional evidence needed to arrange transport.
